A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 13-page documents, including Appendices A–B. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison; the supplementary pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original model comparisons for few-shot classification and image retrieval, cosine-similarity analyses, a BDD100k ablation and supplementary visualization and captioning experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies, with revised one-shot LDA results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The proposed PCA projection remains unchanged: derive principal components from ImageNet class-name text embeddings, retain d/2 components and compare projected image embeddings. No algorithmic revision accompanies the changed LDA scores.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Dogs vs Cats, the 11 classification benchmarks, ROxford/RParis and BDD100k weather/time-of-day evaluation. Removing the BDD100k sentence from Section 4.1 does not remove its experiments, which remain in Section 4.4 and Figure 10.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–3 and Figure 6, including the prototype/LDA classifiers and comparisons involving OTI, CODER, TIP-X and APE. Revised scores do not introduce or remove comparison methods.

E3.justification: The reported models, shot counts, classification and retrieval settings, accuracy/mAP metrics and projection configuration remain unchanged. Neither PDF describes a protocol revision explaining the updated one-shot LDA results.

E4.justification: The similarity-distribution analyses, BDD100k ablation, projection/mean-adjustment visualizations and captioning case studies are retained. The added information-loss sentence introduces no new analysis or evidence.

E5.justification: There are no additions or revisions to repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures. Table 2 changes point estimates only.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces all 2.3% one-shot LDA entries with CLIP 43.4 (50.7), SigLIP 57.3 (62.1), SigLIP2 58.0 (63.4) and DINOv2 59.6; parentheses denote PCA-projected results. These now match the corresponding prototype scores. The revision is confined to this setting; other numerical and qualitative results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The recovery arguments and assumptions in Section 3.1 and Appendix A, and the projection and mean-adjustment derivations in Appendix B, are unchanged. Equations (1)–(12) are retained without mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same principal claims about constrained intra-modal similarities, unreliable misalignment indicators and task ambiguity explaining performance. The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds that information loss through projection is harmful on BDD100k, but this explanation already appears in v1's Figure 10 caption. The task-ambiguity interpretation, applicability boundaries and qualifications in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a direct GitHub code-repository link with a GitHub Pages project-page link, changing the resource-access instructions. Other technical disclosures are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether actual resource availability differs.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. BDD100k reference [45] moves from Section 4.1 to Section 4.4, with its reference-list backlink updated accordingly.

P1.justification: Small edits replace the abstract's code-link wording, shorten the dataset overview and restate the projection information-loss explanation in the ablation paragraph. Section ordering and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 and Table 2 shift within their pages, with accompanying paragraph and column reflow. Table 2 updates best-score underlining for the revised one-shot results. Figure content, table structures and supplementary layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The substantive revision is Table 2's unexplained replacement of uniform 2.3% one-shot LDA scores with values matching the prototype results. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects reporting or reflects changed computation, so the higher scores alone do not establish improved reliability. The remaining edits provide limited presentation changes and repeat an existing interpretation, leaving the overall quality direction uncertain.
